def test_unique_digits():
    # Basic mixed case
    assert unique_digits([15, 33, 1422, 1]) == [1, 15, 33]

    # No elements with all odd digits
    assert unique_digits([152, 323, 1422, 10]) == []

    # Empty input list
    assert unique_digits([]) == []

    # Single element
    assert unique_digits([7]) == [7]

    # All even digits
    assert unique_digits([2, 4, 6, 8]) == []

    # Multi-digit number with all odd digits
    assert unique_digits([13579]) == [13579]

    # All elements qualify; check sorting order
    assert unique_digits([11, 13, 3, 5, 7]) == [3, 5, 7, 11, 13]

    # Contains every digit (evens present)
    assert unique_digits([123456789]) == []

    # Mixed qualifying and non-qualifying
    assert unique_digits([9, 91, 913, 246]) == [9, 91, 913]

    # Zero is even, so excluded
    assert unique_digits([0, 1]) == [1]

    # Zero inside a number disqualifies it
    assert unique_digits([100, 101, 111]) == [111]

    # Duplicates are preserved
    assert unique_digits([3, 3, 5]) == [3, 3, 5]

    # Result is always sorted ascending
    result = unique_digits([33, 1, 5, 9])
    assert result == sorted(result) == [1, 5, 9, 33]
